findings.description: normalize.ts accepts any positive number for analytics.triggered_at and eventito.timestamp (z.number().positive()) and returns it unchanged when >= 1e11. Ingest.eventBody then calls formatUtc(new Date(ms).toISOString()), which throws RangeError for values beyond +/-8.64e15 ms. pushReceived is documented as never throwing, but the throw happens synchronously in #queueEvent before the outbox write. PushListener's try/catch only logs ring_push_not_handed_over, so the event is dropped without being counted as push_unusable. Ring's payload is untrusted (FR-033), so Normalize should treat an out-of-range time as absent and fall back to the next source or received time. Far-future but valid values are also not clamped. I did not check whether a test covers this.
findings.title: Out-of-range Ring timestamp makes a push unqueueable (RangeError)

summary: Partial review. The controller's governance check passed (exit 0). I read the production source for areas 1-3 (push listener, normalize, outbox store, ingest, subscriptions store, callback transport) and the review-preparation document. I did not open the tests, public-contract.test.ts, the plan, tasks.md or the tools schema, so area 4 (contract) and the test-to-code conclusions are unverified. One minor finding is established: Ring-supplied timestamps are not range-checked, so an absurd value makes the event unqueueable. Otherwise the code read matches its stated design: events are held until acked, resends are ordered, the catch-up marker is a barrier, subscriptions are sealed and expire, and the callback transport checks host, HTTPS, no redirects and resolved public addresses at connect time.
